title: The Empire That Didn't Fall
objective: After this level you can explain how the Eastern Roman Empire lasted until 1453.
summary: The Greek-speaking East called itself Roman. Justinian won back Italy and built Hagia Sophia; Constantinople fell to the Ottomans in 1453.

cards.headline: The Roman Empire lasted until 1453, if you count the East.
cards.body: The eastern half, ruled from Constantinople, outlived the West by nearly a thousand years. So when did Rome really end? Depends which half you ask.

cards.headline: Romans in the East
cards.body: Historians call the Eastern Roman Empire the Byzantine Empire. That’s our label, not theirs: its people called themselves Romans. Their capital was Constantinople, which Constantine dedicated in 330 CE. Over time, though, Greek replaced Latin as the language of its government. So picture it: Romans, running the Roman Empire, in Greek.

mascot.line: “Byzantine” is our label. Its people simply called themselves Romans.

cards.headline: Justinian’s ambition
cards.body: In the 6th century CE, the emperor Justinian reconquered Italy and North Africa, for a time. The old West was briefly Roman again. He also had Roman law collected into the Corpus Juris Civilis, the “body of civil law.” And he built the great church of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople, finished in 537 CE. Land, law and a landmark: not a bad record for a “fallen” empire.

cards.context: Sultan Mehmed II led the Ottoman capture of the city, more than a thousand years after Constantine dedicated it in 330 CE. That’s the last page of Roman history, if you count the East. The city itself carried on under a new name: today it’s Istanbul.

cards.headline: The East: endured
learned: Greek became the language of government
Justinian reconquered Italy for a time

questions.prompt: What did the people of the “Byzantine” Empire call themselves?

options.label: Greeks
options.rationale: They spoke Greek, but not that.

questions.explanation: Its people called themselves Romans; “Byzantine” is a later historians’ label.

questions.prompt: Which language came to run the eastern empire’s government?
questions.explanation: Over time Greek replaced Latin as the language of government in the East.

questions.prompt: From Level 77: what did Justinian have Roman law collected into?
questions.explanation: Justinian’s Corpus Juris Civilis became the base of the world’s civil law systems.
